# Leaf

> Leaf is a free, open-source ebook reader for macOS. It opens EPUB, MOBI and AZW3 files directly from Finder without importing them into a library, remembers where you stopped reading, and quits when you close the window. Requires macOS 15 or later. MIT License.

Leaf is built with SwiftUI and WebKit and uses foliate-js to parse and paginate books. It deliberately has no bookshelf or library: you double-click a file, read, and close the window. MOBI and AZW3 files must be DRM-free; books bought from the Kindle Store usually carry DRM and cannot be opened.

## Key facts

- Formats: EPUB, MOBI, AZW3 (DRM-free)
- Platform: macOS 15 or later; universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs
- Price: free; source code under the MIT License
- Download: about 2.4 MB DMG
- Reading position: remembered per book, identified by file content (survives renaming or moving)
- Contents sidebar: native macOS sidebar, toggled with ⌘T, highlights the current chapter
- Typography: font size 80–200% (⌘= / ⌘- / ⌘0), three line-spacing presets, original / sans / serif fonts
- First launch: Leaf is not notarized by Apple; allow it once in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway

## How it compares

- Apple Books: built into macOS and opens EPUB and PDF, but does not import MOBI or AZW3, and adds books to its library.
- Calibre: opens MOBI, AZW3 and EPUB and is centered on library management (about 350 MB download, macOS 14+, GPL-3.0); its viewer can also be launched on its own.
- Leaf: opens all three formats without a library, in a 2.4 MB app.
